name: causal_expert_prefetch_bound_v1

causality.pass_condition: maximum measured host-expert-id-ready to native expert-dispatch-ready interval is smaller than the fastest measured time to transfer one expert object
causality.runtime_dependency: exact routed IDs are materialized on the host immediately before the single native quant_method.apply dispatch for that router batch
causality.causal_lower_bound: max(original candidate lower bound, all-resident LPDDR service plus fastest measured QD expert-storage service for that candidate's unavoidable expert miss bytes)

claim_boundary: This amendment tests the pinned host-driven Qwen runtime in which exact routed expert IDs become host-visible immediately before one native expert-dispatch call for the router batch. When the predeclared causal gate passes, unavoidable cold-expert storage service is treated as preceding that native dispatch rather than as arbitrarily prefetchable beneath it. PLE perfect-prefetch remains allowed. This does not establish a general impossibility of learned expert prediction, speculative execution, GPUDirect Storage, split-batch expert execution, or another redesigned scheduler; those are separate architectures and are not measured here. The amendment is gap-falsification only and cannot establish conventional-memory sufficiency without realizable measured page-cache/scheduler evidence.
